description: We are a team of six students passionate about space technology, AI/ML, electronics, and scientific research. For “Flame in Freefall,” we aim to use NASA’s microgravity combustion data and AI to understand flame behavior and generate insights for improving fire safety in space missions. 🚀🔥
summary:
**FLARE-X (Fire Research, Analysis & Experimental Intelligence Platform)** is an interactive research platform developed to organize, explore, compare, and analyze experimental fire and combustion research, with a particular focus on microgravity and reduced-gravity environments.

The platform integrates 2,504 indexed research records into a unified dashboard featuring an Experiment Library, Comparison Lab, Research Assistant, Knowledge Graph, Research Gap Matrix, Prediction Explorer, and CSV/JSON Data Ingestion system.

FLARE-X addresses the challenge of fragmented experimental research data by providing a centralized environment where researchers can search experimental records, examine parameters such as fuel material, oxygen concentration, pressure and gravity conditions, compare available measurements, and identify underrepresented combinations within the indexed collection.

Its importance lies in making specialized combustion research more accessible, supporting evidence-based research exploration, and helping researchers identify potential directions for future experiments. Data provenance and scientific guardrails are incorporated to distinguish documented evidence from incomplete or unverified information.

**FLARE-X aims to advance accessible, organized, and responsible exploration of fire research.**
details:
FLARE-X: Fire Research, Analysis & Experimental Intelligence Platform

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

FLARE-X is an interactive research platform developed to organize, explore, compare and analyze experimental fire and combustion research, particularly in microgravity and reduced-gravity environments.

The platform brings 2,504 indexed research records into a centralized dashboard. It provides several integrated modules:

  • Platform Overview: Presents an overview of the indexed research collection.
  • Experiment Library: Enables users to search and explore experimental records.
  • Comparison Lab: Supports comparison of experimental conditions and available measurements.
  • Research Assistant: Provides an interactive interface for exploring research information.
  • Knowledge Graph: Visualizes relationships between experimental records and research parameters.
  • Research Gap Matrix: Identifies represented and underrepresented combinations of experimental conditions within the indexed collection.
  • Prediction Explorer: Provides an interface for exploring experimental parameters and potential trends.
  • Data Ingestion & Import: Allows users to upload CSV and JSON datasets, map fields, validate records and import research data.
  • Data Provenance & Guardrails: Helps users understand the origin, completeness and verification status of research information.

The platform organizes information such as fuel materials, oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, gravity conditions and measured experimental variables.

2. What benefits does it provide?

FLARE-X reduces the difficulty of exploring fragmented experimental research information by bringing multiple research records into one interactive environment.

Its benefits include:

  • Faster discovery of relevant experimental records.
  • Easier comparison of experimental conditions.
  • Improved accessibility of specialized combustion research.
  • Identification of potentially underrepresented experimental conditions.
  • Structured organization of scientific datasets.
  • Support for research planning and hypothesis development.
  • Greater awareness of data quality and provenance.

It also provides a framework for expanding the research collection through structured data ingestion.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact of FLARE-X is to support more accessible, organized and responsible exploration of fire and combustion research.

It aims to help researchers, students and developers understand existing experimental knowledge, investigate research coverage and identify potential directions for future experiments.

In the longer term, FLARE-X aims to become an extensible research platform that can accommodate additional experimental datasets, analytical capabilities and research contributions.

The platform may be particularly useful in research areas involving spacecraft fire safety, material flammability, flame spread, combustion behaviour and reduced-gravity environments.

4. What tools, programming languages and software were used?

The platform was developed using accessible web technologies:

  • HTML5: Structures the dashboard and its interface.
  • CSS3: Provides styling, layouts and visual presentation.
  • JavaScript: Implements dashboard interactions, data processing, search, validation and application functionality.
  • JSON: Stores and organizes experimental research records.
  • CSV: Supports structured research data imports.
  • Git and GitHub: Used for source-code version control and project management.
  • GitHub Pages: Hosts the publicly accessible dashboard.
  • Visual Studio Code: Used as the development environment.
  • Python: Used for supporting data inspection and processing tasks.

The project was developed as a web-based application that can be accessed through a browser.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creativity of FLARE-X lies in bringing several research exploration capabilities together in a single specialized platform.

Instead of functioning as a conventional research database, it combines searchable experimental records, comparative analysis, relationship visualization, research gap exploration, predictive interfaces and structured data ingestion.

The Research Gap Matrix is particularly useful because it examines combinations of experimental parameters rather than simply displaying the number of available records.

The platform also incorporates data provenance and scientific guardrails to distinguish missing information, incomplete metadata and unverified records. This encourages responsible interpretation rather than treating every indexed record as equally validated.

Its modular architecture provides a foundation for future expansion as new research datasets and analytical methods become available.

6. What factors were considered during development?

Several important factors guided the development of FLARE-X:

  • Scientific accuracy: Avoiding unsupported conclusions from incomplete or unverified research records.
  • Data integrity: Preserving original experimental fields, measurements and provenance during data ingestion.
  • Data quality: Identifying missing fields, missing units and duplicate identifiers.
  • Accessibility: Creating a browser-based interface that researchers can access without specialized software.
  • Scalability: Supporting expansion beyond the initial indexed research collection.
  • Usability: Organizing complex scientific information into understandable dashboard modules.
  • Transparency: Distinguishing documented information from unverified or incomplete records.
  • Open collaboration: Hosting the project publicly on GitHub to encourage future development and research contributions.

Conclusion

FLARE-X is an effort to connect experimental fire research with interactive data exploration and research intelligence. By combining centralized data organization, comparison tools, research gap exploration and scientific provenance awareness, the platform aims to make specialized combustion research easier to access, understand and investigate.

FLARE-X — Exploring the Frontiers of Fire Research.
